propositions.text: The claimant is a Colombian citizen claiming refugee protection under IRPA sections 96, 97(1)(a) and 97(1)(b).
propositions.quote: XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX is a citizen of Colombia. She claims for refugee protection pursuant to Sections 96, 97(1)(a) and 97(1)(b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The claimant is a Colombian citizen seeking refugee protection under IRPA sections 96, 97(1)(a) and 97(1)(b).

propositions.text: The claimant alleges active involvement in Colombian politics and problems with FARC starting in 1987 due to refusal to help them.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleges she was actively involved in Colombian politics. Her problems with the Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionaries de Colombia (FARC) guerrillas began in 1987 while she was working as a XXXXX XXXXX. The FARC demanded that she XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX She told them that she had no authority to help them in that area.

propositions.text: In 1988, FARC demanded resignations; after killings of those who refused, claimant ended working as City Councillor in 1989.
propositions.quote: In 1988, the FARC demanded that XXXXX XXXXX, including her, resign from their positions. When the FARC began killing XXXXX XXXXX who failed to meet their demands, the claimant ended working as a City Councillor in 1989.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges political involvement and FARC threats starting 1987, leading to resignation as City Councillor in 1989.

propositions.text: In 1993, FARC confiscated claimant's property; in 1995, she received threats demanding resignation or death.
propositions.quote: In 1993, the FARC confiscated the claimant's XXXXX XXXXX with its contents. Subsequently, in 1995, when she became a XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, she began receiving threatening letters from the FARC demanding that she resign from her position or die.

propositions.text: In 1997, her home was bombed and colleague murdered by FARC; she resigned and relocated to Bogota but maintained her position.
propositions.quote: In 1997, her home in XXXXX XXXXX was bombed and, six months later, her colleague, XXXXX XXXXX, was murdered by the FARC. As a result of her colleague's murder, she resigned from her position in the XXXXX XXXXX and permanently located in Bogota. She maintained her XXXXX XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges FARC confiscated property in 1993, threatened her in 1995, bombed her home and murdered colleague in 1997, prompting resignation and relocation.

propositions.text: In 1999, after government-FARC demilitarized zone agreement, claimant returned to XXXXX XXXXX.
propositions.quote: In 1999, after the Colombian government reached an agreement to create a demilitarized zone for the FARC, she returned to XXXXX XXXXX.

propositions.text: In 2001, claimant filed denunciation against FARC for threats and extortion; in 2002, filed another denunciation for threats related to tenant dispute.
propositions.quote: In 2001, the claimant, accompanied with XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, filed a denunciation against the FARC for continued threats and extortion demands. In XXXXX 2002, she filed a denunciation against the FARC with the Public Prosecutor's office in Bogota for threats made against her when her tenant, backed by the FARC, refused to vacate her house in XXXXX XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges returning in 1999 and filing denunciations against FARC in 2001 and 2002 for threats and extortion.

propositions.text: The key issues are whether the claimant has subjective fear and whether that fear is objectively well-founded.
propositions.quote: The determinative issues in this case are subjective and whether, at this time, her fear is objectively well-founded.

propositions.text: The panel finds claimant lacks subjective fear and her fear is not objectively well-founded.
propositions.quote: Based on the evidence adduced, the panel does not find that the claimant has a subjective fear of persecution in Colombia, as well as her fear is not objectively well-founded.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant lacks subjective fear and her fear is not objectively well-founded.

propositions.text: Testimony under oath is presumed true unless valid reason to doubt; truth judged by harmony with probabilities.
propositions.quote: With regard to credibility, the panel is aware that testimony given under oath is presumed to be true, unless there is a valid reason to doubt its truthfulness.1 The panel is also aware that the real test of the truth of a story of a witness is that it be in harmony with the preponderance of probabilities which a practical and informed person would readily recognise as reasonable in that place and in those conditions.2

propositions.text: Evidence must be probably true, not just possibly true, to be credible or trustworthy.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the panel cannot be satisfied that, "the evidence is credible or trustworthy unless satisfied that it is probably so, not just possibly so".3

paragraphs.summary: The panel states testimony is presumed true unless doubted and must be probably true to be credible.

propositions.text: After reviewing all evidence, the panel finds claimant lacks subjective fear which is not objectively well-founded.
propositions.quote: Based on the totality of the evidence adduced, the panel finds that the claimant lacked subjective fear which is not objectively well-founded.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant lacks subjective fear and her fear is not objectively well-founded after reviewing all evidence.

propositions.text: Claimant fears FARC; problems began in 1987 but she did not leave Colombia until 2003.
propositions.quote: In this case, the claimant indicated that she fears the FARC guerrilla group in Colombia. She indicated that her problems with the FARC began in 1987 but she did not leave Colombia until 2003.

propositions.text: In 2002, claimant applied for refugee protection in Canadian Embassy in Bogota but was refused; fled to Italy in 2003.
propositions.quote: She testified that in 2002 she applied for refugee protection at the Canadian Embassy in Bogota. When her application for refugee protection was refused, she decided to flee to Italy in XXXXX 2003.

propositions.text: She lived temporarily in Italy until 2007, then returned to Colombia despite fearing persecution, expecting peace talks to succeed.
propositions.quote: She lived in Italy on a temporary status until XXXXX 2007 and thereafter she decided to return to Colombia, the country where she feared persecution at the hands of the FARC. She indicated that she did not apply for asylum in Italy because she intended to return to Colombia expecting the peace talks between the FARC and the Colombian Government to succeed.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant feared FARC since 1987 but stayed in Colombia until 2003, applied for refugee protection in 2002, fled to Italy, then returned expecting peace talks to succeed.

propositions.text: Claimant's expectation to return after peace talks is unreasonable as talks collapsed in 2002 before she left for Italy.
propositions.quote: Her expectations to return to Colombia after peace talks between the Government of Colombia and the FARC succeeded are not reasonable since peace talks between the two parties had collapsed in XXXXX of 2002,4 before she left to go to Italy.

propositions.text: Long stay in Italy without asylum claim and return to Colombia indicate lack of subjective fear of persecution by FARC.
propositions.quote: The panel finds that the claimant's long stay in Italy, without making an attempt to file for asylum, and her return to Colombia is indicative of lack of subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant's return after peace talks collapsed and no asylum claim in Italy indicate lack of subjective fear of FARC persecution.

propositions.text: Six to seven months stay in Colombia before returning to Italy indicates lack of subjective fear of FARC persecution.
propositions.quote: Her six to seven months' stay in Colombia is indicative of lack of subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC.

propositions.text: Failure to claim asylum in Italy during second visit and return to Colombia again indicate lack of subjective fear.
propositions.quote: Once she returned to Italy, she failed to make an asylum claim in that country. Her failure to make an asylum claim during her second visit to Italy is another example of lack of subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia. Her return to Colombia where she feared the FARC for the second time also indicates that she lacked subjective fear of persecution in that country.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant's stays in Colombia and Italy without asylum claims and returns to Colombia show lack of subjective fear of FARC persecution.

propositions.text: Claimant left Colombia for Mexico in 2008 due to continued FARC threats, lived with daughter, then returned to Colombia.
propositions.quote: After she returned to Colombia from Italy, threats from the FARC continued and as a result she decided to go to Mexico in XXXXX of 2008. In Mexico, she lived with her daughter until XXXXX, 2008 before returning to Colombia.

propositions.text: Failure to seek asylum in Mexico despite FARC threats and returning to Colombia to get US visas indicates lack of subjective fear.
propositions.quote: She indicated that she did not file for asylum in Mexico because she had no plans to do so since she was only visiting her daughter. Since she was allegedly threatened by the FARC in Colombia, her failure to seek asylum in Mexico, a country signatory to refugee Convention, indicates that she lacked subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia. Her reason for returning to obtain USA visas from the USA embassy in Colombia is not reasonable since she could have obtained those visas at the USA embassy in Mexico. Her return to Colombia on XXXXX 2008 is another example of lack of subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant's failure to seek asylum in Mexico and return to Colombia for US visas despite FARC threats shows lack of subjective fear.

propositions.text: After getting US visas, claimant returned to Mexico in 2009, made no attempt to regularize status, then went to Las Vegas and Canada.
propositions.quote: After receiving the USA visas, she returned to Mexico in XXXXX 2009. Once again she made no attempt to regularize her status in Mexico. Her actions indicate her lack of subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia. From Mexico she went to Las Vegas and then to Canada.

propositions.text: Claimant did not plan to apply for asylum in USA because she wanted to join her brother in Canada.
propositions.quote: She indicated that she did not plan to apply for asylum in the USA because she wanted to join her brother in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant's failure to regularize status in Mexico and no asylum claim in USA, aiming to join brother in Canada, shows lack of subjective fear.

propositions.text: Claimant's brother has been Canadian resident since 2003 and successful refugee applicant; claimant knew about Canadian refugee protection.
propositions.quote: The claimant's brother is a resident of Canada since 2003. He was a successful refugee applicant. The claimant had knowledge about the refugee protection in Canada since she had applied for refugee protection at the Canadian embassy in Bogota in 2002.

propositions.text: Despite brother's status and contact, claimant made no effort to come to Canada earlier, choosing Italy and Mexico instead, indicating lack of subjective fear.
propositions.quote: Although her brother had status in Canada since 2003, and, given that she was in contact with him since he left Colombia, the claimant made no effort to come to Canada to regularize her status earlier. She chose to go to Italy and Mexico instead. Her actions indicate lack of subjective fear of persecution from the FARC in Colombia.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant knew about Canadian refugee protection and brother's status but delayed coming to Canada, indicating lack of subjective fear.

propositions.text: Claimant's behaviour and actions indicate lack of subjective fear of FARC persecution after 1997 resignation.
propositions.quote: Based on the evidence adduced, the claimant's behaviour and her actions indicate that she lacked subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia. The panel is not persuaded to believe that she feared the FARC after she resigned from her XXXXX XXXXX position in 1997.

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes claimant's behaviour shows lack of subjective fear of FARC persecution after 1997 resignation.

propositions.text: Claimant testified to continuous FARC threats after 1997 resignation and personal contact by FARC commander.
propositions.quote: Moreover, the claimant testified that she was continuously threatened by the FARC, after she resigned from her position as a member of XXXXX XXXXX She also indicated that on one occasion she was personally contacted by the commander of the FARC from XXXXX XXXXX.

propositions.text: Claimant provided no documentary evidence or affidavits to corroborate threats after 1997 resignation despite instruction to do so.
propositions.quote: At the hearing she did not provide any documentary evidence, such as a police report or an affidavit, to indicate that she was threatened by the FARC after her resignation from the XXXXX XXXXX in 1997. She did not provide media articles and/or affidavits either from her daughter in Colombia or from other colleagues and friends to corroborate that she was threatened by the FARC after she left her XXXXX XXXXX position. Also she did not provide persuasive reasons for failing to provide such documents to help the panel in its decision. The onus is on her to establish her claim particularly when she was instructed in question 31 to provide documentary evidence to establish her claim.

paragraphs.summary: The panel notes claimant testified to threats after 1997 but provided no documentary evidence despite instructions, raising doubts.

propositions.text: Failure to provide documentary evidence raises serious doubt about FARC's interest to harm claimant after resignation.
propositions.quote: Her failure to provide the aforementioned documentary evidence raises a serious doubt in the panel's mind as to whether the FARC had any further interest to harm the claimant when she resigned from the XXXXX XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds failure to provide evidence raises serious doubt about FARC's interest to harm claimant after resignation.

propositions.text: Since claimant complied with FARC demand to resign, panel is not persuaded FARC had interest to harm her after that.
propositions.quote: Also the FARC demanded that she resign from her position at the XXXXX XXXXX which she did. As a result, the panel is not persuaded to believe that the FARC had any interest to harm her after she complied with their demands.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant fabricated story about threats after 1997 to bolster refugee claim.
propositions.quote: The panel finds that the claimant has fabricated her story about threats from the FARC after 1997 to bolster her refugee claim.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant complied with FARC demands and fabricated post-1997 threats to bolster claim.

propositions.text: Panel does not believe FARC threatened claimant after 1997 resignation and finds no objectively well-founded fear of persecution.
propositions.quote: Based on the evidence adduced, the panel does not believe that the FARC threatened the claimant after she resigned from her position at the XXXXX XXXXX in 1997 because they had no interest to do so. As a result, the panel does not find that the claimant has an objectively well-founded fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds no credible threats after 1997 and no objectively well-founded fear of persecution by FARC.

propositions.text: Professor Hathaway states protracted postponement of refugee claim is relevant to evaluating sincerity of need for protection.
propositions.quote: Professor Hathaway has said that it is appropriate to inquire into the circumstances of any protracted postponement of a refugee claim as a means of evaluating the sincerity of the claimant's need for protection.5

paragraphs.summary: Professor Hathaway states delay in refugee claim is relevant to assessing sincerity of protection need.

propositions.text: In Leon, Federal Court found claimant's five-year delay in refugee claim was incredible and undermined credibility.
propositions.quote: In Leon, the claimant waited over five years to make a claim. Justice Muldoon of the Federal Court commented: It is incredible that he [the claimant] would believe that he could not make a refugee claim because he was an illegal ........ That is incredible. That he would wait for 5 years in that belief, if that belief were true, is even more incredible.6

paragraphs.summary: In Leon, Federal Court found five-year delay in refugee claim undermined claimant's credibility.

propositions.text: Claimant lacked subjective fear of persecution by the FARC and her fear is not objectively well-founded
propositions.quote: because the claimant lacked subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC, and since her fear is not objectively well-founded

propositions.text: There is less than a mere possibility that claimant would be persecuted by the FARC if returned to Colombia
propositions.quote: there is less than a mere possibility that she would be persecuted by the FARC should she return to Colombia

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant lacks subjective and objective fear of persecution by the FARC and that persecution is less than a mere possibility if returned to Colombia.

propositions.text: Credibility findings apply to claimant's assertion of risk to life or cruel treatment in Colombia
propositions.quote: The panel's credibility findings also apply to the claimant's assertion that she faces a risk to his life or of being subjected to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment in Colombia

propositions.text: Claimant lacks subjective fear and her fear is not objectively well-founded
propositions.quote: Since the claimant lacks subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC, and her fear is not objectively well-founded

propositions.text: Claimant does not face risk to life, cruel treatment, or torture if returned to Colombia
propositions.quote: the panel finds that the claimant does not face a risk to her life or to being subjected to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment or to a danger of being tortured, should she return to Colombia

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant's credibility issues apply to her risk claims and that she does not face risk to life or cruel treatment if returned.

propositions.text: Review of all documentary evidence shows no persuasive evidence of risk beyond general violence in Colombia
propositions.quote: Based on the documentary evidence, there is no persuasive evidence to indicate that, at this time, the claimant will be subjected to any other risk, other than the risk of general violence which all citizens in Colombia are subjected to

paragraphs.summary: The court finds documentary evidence shows no risk to claimant beyond general violence in Colombia.

propositions.text: Claimant is not a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection under IRPA sections 97(1)(a) and 97(1)(b)
propositions.quote: the panel finds that the claimant is not a Convention refugee, nor she is a person in need of protection pursuant to sections 97(1)(a) and 97(1)(b) of the IRPA

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor in need of protection under IRPA sections 97(1)(a) and (b).

propositions.text: Refugee Protection Division rejects claimant's refugee protection claim
propositions.quote: the Refugee Protection Division rejects the claim of XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX for refugee protection

paragraphs.summary: The court orders rejection of claimant's refugee protection claim.
